newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian car bombs kill 20, threat of more to come.
newsitem.headline: Algerian car bombs kill 20, threat of more to come.

text.p: An Algerian rebel leader has threatened a wave of bomb attacks after two car bombs exploded hours apart in Algeria on Tuesday killing 20 people and wounding at least 111, Algerian newspapers said on Wednesday.
A huge car bomb exploded in central Algiers on Tuesday near the main university faculty, killing 13 people and wounding at least 100, Liberte newspaper said, quoting hospital sources.
Another car bomb went off some hours later in Ain-Fakroun town in the eastern province of Oum el Bouaghi, 380-km (237- miles) east of Algiers, killing seven and wounding 11, Al Khabar newspaper said.
Algerian authorities, without mentioning the Ain-Fakroun bombing, said seven people were killed and more than 40 wounded in the Algiers blast.
Security forces had defused in the past week about 17 devices and cars laden with explosives set to explode in Algiers and surrounding towns, El Watan newspaper said.
Liberte newspaper said the authorities had identified guerrilla Farid Hamani, alias Abu Salmane, as the mastermind behind the bombings.

The newspaper said 27-year-old Hamani was a veteran guerrilla who took part in the first rebel attacks in Algiers early in 1992 after the authorities cancelled a general election which radical Islamists were poised to win.
El Watan said Hamani had warned in a New Year's eve statement that the guerrillas had prepared about 50 bombs to be detonated in Algiers.
Liberte said Hamani was behind two bomb attacks late in December in the Algerian capital in which at least 18 people died.
Algiers has been the target of numerous bomb attacks in recent years.

The worst in the crowded city of some four million people was in 1995 when Moslem rebels slammed a stolen car laden with explosives into Algiers' main police station killing more than 40 people and wounding more than 300.
The Islamic Armed Group (GIA) claimed responsibility for the attack and said it had hundred of volunteers ready for more suicide bomb attacks.
Liberte said Hamani is a GIA gang leader in Algiers.
The bombings follow rebel raids against villages in which 200 people were killed in the past two-and-a-half months, many of them having their throats slit.
The guerrillas, in the latest massacre of villagers, stormed Douaouda hamlet, 60-km (37-miles) west of Algiers, on Sunday night killing 18 people, including a six-months-old baby.
Rebels broke into a real-estate office on the same night killing the director, two women employees and one woman customer in Ain Benian district, on the northern edge of Algiers.
Sixteen villagers were slaughtered in a raid in Ben Achour village, 50-km (30-miles) south of Algiers on Saturday night.
About 60,000 people, civilians, Moslem militants and security forces, have died since 1992.
